title: A first-quadrant spectral sequence concentrated in the row q = 0 collapses
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $(E_r^{p,q},d_r)_{r\ge2}$ be a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence in $\mathcal A$: $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p\ge0$ and $q\ge0$, $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$, $d_r\circ d_r=0$ and $E_{r+1}\cong\ker d_r/\operatorname{im}d_r$. Suppose it converges to a sequence of objects $(H^n)_{n\ge0}$ of $\mathcal A$: each $H^n$ carries a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq F^1H^n\supseteq\dots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$ with $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$, where $E_\infty^{p,q}=E_r^{p,q}$ for $r>\max(p,q+1)$. If $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for every $q>0$, then for every $n\ge0$ the edge map $E_2^{n,0}=E_\infty^{n,0}=F^nH^n\hookrightarrow H^n$ is an isomorphism $E_2^{n,0}\cong H^n$. In particular, if moreover $H^n=0$ for every $n>0$, then $E_2^{n,0}=0$ for every $n>0$.

source.place: Homology, Definition 011O (label definition-limit-spectral-sequence: degeneration at $E_r$ and $E_r=E_\infty$) and Lemma 0132 (label lemma-first-quadrant-ss: first-quadrant spectral sequences are bounded and converge with finite filtrations); used without statement in Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, second paragraph ("Using the spectral sequence ... we conclude")

proof.text: **Step 1 (the vanishing propagates to every page).** Claim: for every $r\ge2$, $E_r^{p,q}=0$ whenever $p<0$, or $q<0$, or $q>0$. For $r=2$ this is the first-quadrant hypothesis together with the hypothesis $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q>0$. If it holds for $r$, then $E_{r+1}^{p,q}\cong\ker(d_r^{p,q})/\operatorname{im}(d_r^{p-r,q+r-1})$ is a subquotient of $E_r^{p,q}$, and a subquotient of $0$ is $0$ in the abelian category $\mathcal A$; so it holds for $r+1$. By induction on $r$ the claim holds for all $r\ge2$.

source.place: Definition 011N (definition-spectral-sequence, line 5164): $E_{r+1}=\Ker(d_r)/\Im(d_r)$; Lemma 0BDV (lemma-relate-boundedness, line 6292), proof hint: 'If $E_r^{p,q}=0$, then we have $E_{r'}^{p,q}=0$ for all $r'\ge r$'

proof.text: **Step 2 ($E_\infty$ and the row $q=0$ is stationary from $E_2$ on).** Fix $(p,q)$ and $r>\max(p,q+1)$. The differential out of $E_r^{p,q}$ lands in $E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ with $q-r+1<0$, and the differential into it starts at $E_r^{p-r,q+r-1}$ with $p-r<0$; both objects are $0$ by Step 1, so both differentials are $0$ and $E_{r+1}^{p,q}\cong\ker/\operatorname{im}=E_r^{p,q}$. Hence the $E_r^{p,q}$ for $r>\max(p,q+1)$ are identified with each other by these isomorphisms, and $E_\infty^{p,q}$ of the statement is well defined (in Stacks' terms the subobjects $Z_r^{p,q}$, $B_r^{p,q}$ of $E_2^{p,q}$ are stationary, so this is the limit $Z_\infty/B_\infty$; a first-quadrant spectral sequence is bounded, hence regular and coregular). Now take $(p,q)=(n,0)$ with $n\ge0$ and any $r\ge2$: the differential out of $E_r^{n,0}$ lands in $E_r^{n+r,1-r}$, which is $0$ since $1-r<0$; the differential into $E_r^{n,0}$ starts at $E_r^{n-r,r-1}$, which is $0$ by Step 1 since $r-1\ge1>0$ (the hypothesis on the rows $q>0$). So $d_r$ vanishes into and out of $E_r^{n,0}$ for every $r\ge2$, $E_{r+1}^{n,0}\cong E_r^{n,0}$ for every $r\ge2$, and composing these finitely many isomorphisms up to any $r>\max(n,1)$ gives $E_2^{n,0}\cong E_\infty^{n,0}$.

source.place: Definition 011O (definition-limit-spectral-sequence, line 5219): limit $E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty$ and degeneration at $E_r$ with $E_r=E_{r+1}=\dots=E_\infty$; Definition 0BDU (definition-bounded-ss, line 6262) and Lemma 0BDV (lemma-relate-boundedness, line 6292), (1)-(2), (5)-(6): bounded implies regular and coregular, i.e. $Z_r^{p,q}$ and $B_r^{p,q}$ eventually constant

proof.text: **Step 3 (the filtration of $H^n$ collapses to its last step).** Fix $n\ge0$. By hypothesis $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq\dots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$ with $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$ [def-sp-filtration]. For $0\le p\le n-1$ we have $n-p\ge1$, so $E_\infty^{p,n-p}=E_r^{p,n-p}=0$ (for $r$ large, Step 2) by Step 1. So the inclusion $F^{p+1}H^n\to F^pH^n$ is a monomorphism with cokernel $\operatorname{gr}^pH^n=0$, hence an epimorphism, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-abelian]; i.e. $F^{p+1}H^n=F^pH^n$ as subobjects. Composing for $p=0,\dots,n-1$: $F^nH^n=F^0H^n=H^n$, so the inclusion $F^nH^n\hookrightarrow H^n$ is an isomorphism. Since $F^{n+1}H^n=0$, the quotient map $F^nH^n\to F^nH^n/F^{n+1}H^n=\operatorname{gr}^nH^n$ is an isomorphism, and $\operatorname{gr}^nH^n\cong E_\infty^{n,0}$. (For $n=0$ the chain is empty and $F^0H^0=H^0$ directly.)

source.place: Definition 0121 (definition-filtered, line 4667), items (1), (7): finite filtrations and $\operatorname{gr}^p=F^p/F^{p+1}$; Lemma 012W (lemma-biregular-ss-converges, line 6362), proof of (4): 'we can find an $r'$ such that $E_\infty^{p,q}=E_{r'}^{p,q}$ for all $p,q$ with $p+q=n$. Thus $H^n$ has a finite filtration whose graded pieces are ...'; Lemma 0132 (lemma-first-quadrant-ss, line 6672), (2)-(3): finite filtrations and convergence in the first quadrant

proof.text: **Step 4 (the edge map; the particular case).** The edge map of the statement is the composite $E_2^{n,0}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }E_\infty^{n,0}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{gr}^nH^n=F^nH^n\hookrightarrow H^n$ of the isomorphism of Step 2, the inverse of the convergence isomorphism, the identification $F^nH^n=\operatorname{gr}^nH^n$ (as $F^{n+1}H^n=0$) and the inclusion; each is an isomorphism (Steps 2 and 3), so the edge map is an isomorphism $E_2^{n,0}\cong H^n$ for every $n\ge0$. If moreover $H^n=0$ for every $n>0$, then $E_2^{n,0}\cong H^n=0$ for every $n>0$ (and conversely, if $E_2^{n,0}=0$ for $n>0$ then $H^n=0$ for $n>0$).
